text:
To rummage, sweet Helpide, you clear,

how we remain from so much remaining.


Today you come when I have barely risen.

The stable is divinely pissed

and excremented by the innocent cow

and the innocent ass and the innocent rooster.


Enter the ecumenical Mary.

O saintgabriel, make the soul conceive,

the lightless love, the skyless one,

the most stone, the most nothing,

                   even the monarch illusion.


We will burn all the ships!

We will burn the final essence!


But if one must suffer from myth to myth,

and you arrive to speak to me chewing ice,

let us chew embers;

there is nowhere left to descend,

there is nowhere left to climb.


The rooster has turned uncertain, man.

translation.title: Trilce: Poem XIX - To Rummage, Sweet Helpide, You Clear
translation.editorial_note: The translation keeps Vallejo's irreverent stable imagery, saintgabriel neologism, and final uncertain rooster.
